newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Peres says he will not run for PM.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Peres says he will not run for PM.

text.p: Israeli opposition Labour Party leader Shimon Peres said on Wednesday he would not run for prime minister in the next elections in the year 2000.
"I will not run in the year 2000," Peres, 73, told Israel's Channel One Television.

Peres also said he would not contend for leadership of the Labour party at internal elections slated for July 1997. He emphasised he would continue to fight for the Middle East peace process of which he was a principal architect.
It was the first time that Peres, a winner of the Nobel peace prize for interim peace deals with the Palestinians, had declared he had run for the last time for the highest office in Israel.

Peres, who became prime minister after the assassination of his predecessor Yitzhak Rabin by a right-wing Jew in November, lost elections in May by less then a percentage point to Likud party leader Benjamin Netanyahu. It was the fifth time he failed to win an election for prime minister.
Ehud Barak, 56, a former army chief of staff who served as foreign minister in Peres's government, declared this month he would challenge Peres for the party leadership next July.
